name: Turn Order Queue
description: Whose turn it is, in what order, and when the round rolls over. Initiative is rolled once per combatant at battle start — modified by combat.status_effects, since a slowed unit should act late — then the queue is fixed until someone dies or a delay action inserts them elsewhere. The queue owns sequencing only: what a unit may DO with its turn is combat.action_point_economy's budget, and ending a turn early is the player's call via input.endTurn, not the queue's. Rounds are the queue's second product: combat.roundStarted exists so per-round systems — damage-over-time ticks, reinforcement timers — have exactly one heartbeat to follow instead of everyone counting turns privately and disagreeing.

inputs.name: initiativeDieSides
inputs.description: Die rolled per combatant for initiative. A big die makes order swingy; a small die makes the dex stat king. d20 splits the difference.

inputs.name: allowDelayTurn
inputs.description: Whether a unit may yield to a later slot in the same round. Delay is the entry-level tactics verb; disabling it is a hardcore statement.

inputs.name: tieBreakBy
inputs.description: Attribute consulted on tied initiative rolls. Deterministic tie-breaks keep replays and replays-of-replays identical.

outputs.name: activeUnitId
outputs.description: The unit whose turn is live.

outputs.name: queuePreview
outputs.description: Upcoming order, for the UI timeline players plan against.
